This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so any refundable detour mileage would enter the metered fare (base $3.90 + distance $42.05 for 29.82 km + time $12.35 + waiting $0.11 + platform $1.47 = $59.88) [F7]. The trace settles that there is exactly one off-route segment [F3] and that no RD-4 incident excuses it: the only traffic item on the replaced stretch is the PIE speed band 2 record of 18:00–18:37, which under RD-4(b) is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment on its own, and no incident was recorded near the route at all [F12][F15], the weather being fair [F16]. The remaining question is the scope of the rider's agreement (RD-5), and it is settled by the rider's own words. At 18:35 the driver asked whether to take another way because of the building PIE jam [F8], and at 18:35 — before the segment began at 18:37 — the rider answered "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" [F9]. That is a general route authorization, not a specific named road, so it covers a route chosen to get to Pasir Ris MRT, and it excludes only an errand or a loop of the driver's own [F9][F8][RD-5]. The record shows no stop, no errand and no loop reaching nothing: the segment is a continuous stretch toward the same destination [F3], driven in precisely the window in which the PIE ran at band 2 while the parallel Tampines Expressway ran at band 5 [F12][F13]. Taking a longer-but-faster corridor under "哪条快走哪条" is the choice the rider authorized, so the segment is exempt and its 2.07 km extra is not refundable [F3][F9][F13][RD-5]. There was no rider-named stop, so RD-3 does not exempt or condemn anything here [F9][F3][RD-3]. The driver's after-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally [F11] is not consent, but the rider's own timestamped message [F9] is, so the finding does not rest on the statement [F11][F9][RD-5]. Because every off-route segment is exempt, the amount under the trace's formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4101/km = 0 km × $1.4101/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The only billed excess-distance charge, $3.47 for 2.46 km at $1.4101/km, is the same mileage the exempt segment accounts for, and RD-2 does not refund exempt-segment mileage [F4][F3][RD-2]. The waiting item of $0.11 for 0.4 minutes is the meter's waiting unit, which RD-3(c) charges on RydeTAXI and does not refund [F5][RD-3], and the fare build-up contains no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 adds nothing [F7][FARE-1]. With a refund of $0.00 the outcome is no_action, and although the record still shows a route-deviation finding against the driver (RD-1), no account flag follows, because RD-6 conditions the flag on a refund greater than zero or a recorded RD-1 breach; the trace marks the RD-6 prerequisite only as a prior-dispute profile element (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2) [F18], and a profile fact may not be the sole basis for an account action [F18][RD-6].

Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete with every message timestamped [F10], the fare and distance records are present [F4][F7], and traffic and timeline records cover the segment window [F3][F12], so none of the elements above lacks a record [F3][F4][F7][F10][F12].
